options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians killed in police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes
options.reason: Bars make it easy to compare the exact count for each individual year.
options.interpretation: This directly answers how many pedestrians were killed in each calendar year: the bar heights and labels give the annual counts. A bar chart is defensible because the years are discrete categories and the requested measure is an absolute count. It does not explain causes or provide a population- or exposure-adjusted risk.

options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians killed in police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes
options.reason: A line chart emphasizes how the annual fatality count changes over time while retaining each year's value.
options.interpretation: This answers the annual-count part of the question and makes the year-to-year pattern visible, including a high of 176 in 2013 and a low of 101 in 2020. A line chart is defensible because the years are ordered in time, and the point labels preserve the exact counts. It does not explain causes or provide a population- or exposure-adjusted risk.
